title: Keeping a Sourdough Starter

questions.q: What produces the gas that raises the bread?
questions.e: The yeast makes the gas; the bacteria make the acids.

questions.q: What produces the acids that give the bread its sour taste?
questions.e: Lactic acid bacteria produce the acids.

questions.q: How many hours after a room temperature feed does a healthy starter start to have doubled, at the earliest?
A starter has not doubled in twelve hours. What must happen before it is used?
questions.e: Sluggish starters get two days of regular feeding.
questions.src: needs two days of regular feeding

questions.q: What is the standard feed ratio of starter, flour, and water by weight?
When is a stiff 1:2:1 feed used?
o: When it will sit more than a day
When it fails the float test
When it smells of nail polish
questions.e: A stiff feed slows fermentation for a longer wait.
questions.src: will sit for more than a day

questions.q: Feed water must stay below what temperature?
questions.e: Hotter than 30 degrees Celsius kills the yeast.

questions.q: How often is a refrigerated starter fed?
Gray liquid on top of the starter means what?
o: It is hungry and should be fed sooner
It is ready to bake with
questions.src: hungry and should be fed sooner

questions.q: Which sign means the whole starter must be thrown away?
The starter smells of nail polish remover. Which is true?
o: Overdue for a feed, still safe
questions.e: Overdue but still safe to use.
questions.src: overdue for a feed but is still safe to use

questions.q: A spoonful floats in water. What does the float test say?
questions.e: If it floats, it is ready.
